title: Three Dollars, Thirty Seconds: Why Street Food Wins the City
title_zh: 三美元，三十秒：街头美食为何赢得整座城市
intro_zh: 本文约 572 词，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（vendor, affordable, aroma, authentic, queue, hygiene），句子难度中等，适合快速阅读与细节推断练习。

paragraphs.en: At six in the evening, the street behind the market changes character. Office workers step off buses, students drop their bags, and within ten minutes a row of stalls has turned the pavement into an open-air restaurant. Charcoal glows, oil hisses, and the smell of grilled meat drifts two blocks away. This is street food, and in most of the world's cities it is not a weekend snack but a daily habit.
paragraphs.zh: 傍晚六点，市场后面的那条街换了一副模样。上班族下了公交，学生放下书包，不到十分钟，一排小摊就把人行道变成了一家露天餐厅。炭火发红，油锅滋滋作响，烤肉的香味能飘出两个街区。这就是街头美食——在世界大多数城市里，它不是周末的小零嘴，而是每天的日常。

paragraphs.en: Street food is easy to define: cheap, freshly cooked dishes sold from a cart or a window opening onto the pavement, eaten standing up or on a plastic stool nearby. The vendor cooks in front of you, in a space no bigger than a wardrobe. The Food and Agriculture Organization estimates that about 2.5 billion people eat street food every day — a number that sounds huge until you notice how ordinary the scene is in Bangkok or Chengdu.
paragraphs.zh: 街头美食很容易定义：便宜、现做的食物，从推车或临街的窗口卖出，人们站着吃，或坐在旁边的小塑料凳上吃。摊主就在你面前烹饪，地方还没有一个衣柜大。联合国粮农组织估计，每天大约有 25 亿人吃街头食物——这个数字听起来惊人，直到你发现这样的场景在曼谷或成都多么平常。

paragraphs.en: The first attraction is the price. A bowl of noodles or three skewers of lamb often costs the same as one coffee in a shopping mall. For a young worker renting a small room, street food is affordable in a way that restaurants are not. It is quick as well: three minutes from ordering to the first bite, ten from first bite to last. A one-hour lunch break suddenly becomes enough.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个吸引力是价格。一碗面或三串羊肉串，常常和商场里一杯咖啡同价。对一个租着小房间的年轻上班族来说，街头食物是餐馆给不了的那种实惠。它还快：从点单到第一口三分钟，从第一口到最后一口十分钟。一小时的午休忽然就够用了。

paragraphs.en: Then there is the aroma. Street food reaches the senses before it reaches your mouth. You hear the wok, see the flames, watch the dough stretched by hand, and smell what the person ahead of you is holding. In a restaurant the kitchen is a closed door; at a stall, cooking is a performance and you stand inside it.
paragraphs.zh: 然后还有香气。街头食物在进嘴之前，早就抵达了你的感官。你听见锅铲响，看见火苗，看着面团被手工抻开，闻到排在你前面那个人手里拿着什么。在餐馆里，厨房是一扇关着的门；在摊位前，烹饪是一场表演，而你就站在其中。

paragraphs.en: Skill matters too. Many stalls sell exactly one dish, and the owner has made it thousands of times. In Xi'an, a woman who has pressed the same flatbread for twenty-six years can tell from the sound of the dough whether it needs more water. That focus is rare in any kitchen, and it is why an authentic local taste is hard to copy in a factory.
paragraphs.zh: 手艺也很重要。许多摊位只卖一样东西，而摊主已经做了成千上万次。在西安，一位压了二十六年同一款饼的女士，能凭面团的声音判断它是否还需要加水。这种专注在任何厨房里都少见，也正是正宗的地方味道难以在工厂里复制的原因。

paragraphs.en: Street food is also social glue. Because everyone waits in the same short queue, strangers begin to talk: about the weather, the price, which dish to order. A cook remembers that you dislike coriander; after a month you are a regular; after a year, almost a friend. Researchers say these short exchanges are the weak ties that make a neighbourhood feel safe.
paragraphs.zh: 街头美食还是社会的黏合剂。因为大家在同一条短队里等着，陌生人就开始聊起来：聊天气，聊价钱，聊该点哪一样。摊主会记得你不吃香菜；一个月后你是熟客；一年后，几乎算个朋友。研究者说，正是这些短短的交流构成了让街区显得安全的那些弱联系。

paragraphs.en: The common worry is hygiene, and it deserves respect. The sensible rule is to watch the crowd: a busy stall with high turnover wastes less food and fries everything in front of you, while an empty one may leave ingredients out for hours. Clean hands, hot oil and a short line are usually better signs than a printed certificate on the wall.
paragraphs.zh: 常见的担忧是卫生，这值得认真对待。明智的做法是看人气：生意好、周转快的摊位浪费少，而且一切都在你眼前现炸；空荡荡的摊位则可能把食材摆在外面好几个小时。干净的手、滚烫的油和一条不长的队，通常比墙上一张打印的证书更可信。

paragraphs.en: For visitors, street food is the quickest way to read a city. It explains what grows nearby, what people can afford, and who works late. But success brings problems too: when a stall becomes famous, rents rise and prices follow, and a cook may trade an old recipe for a faster one.
paragraphs.zh: 对游客来说，街头美食是读懂一座城市最快的方式。它说明了当地产什么、人们能负担什么、谁工作到很晚。但成功也带来问题：一个摊位出名之后，租金上涨，价格随之上涨，摊主也可能用更快的做法换掉原来的配方。

paragraphs.en: So the next time you pass a steaming cart, stop and look at who is cooking. Behind that small fire is a person running a business, and behind the queue is a neighbourhood eating together. The best meal in town may cost three dollars and take thirty seconds to hand over.
paragraphs.zh: 所以下次经过一辆冒着热气的小车时，停下来看看是谁在做。那团小火背后，是一个人在做生意；那条队伍背后，是一个街区在一起吃饭。城里最好的一餐，也许只要三美元，递到你手里只要三十秒。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why street food attracts people and matters to city life
Why restaurants are losing customers to food stalls
How to open a successful street food business
The health risks of eating on the pavement
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从价格、香气、手艺、社交功能、卫生与旅游影响等角度说明街头美食的吸引力及其在城市生活中的作用，故选第一项。其余选项或过于片面（只涉及一段），或文中并未讨论。

questions.q: According to the passage, why is a busy stall with high turnover a better choice?
options: It charges much higher prices than other stalls.
It is usually safer because food is cooked freshly in front of you.
It sells only one dish, so the choice is simple.
It provides printed certificates on the wall.
questions.explain: 细节／推断题。第六段指出人气旺的摊位周转快、浪费少、食物在你眼前现炸，作者还认为干净的手、滚烫的油和短队比墙上的证书更可信，因此第二项正确。文中未说人气摊位价格更高，也未把'只卖一样'当作理由。

questions.q: What can be inferred about a cook who has made the same dish for many years?
options: He or she earns more than restaurant chefs.
He or she often changes the recipe to attract tourists.
He or she has a deep and detailed knowledge of that dish.
He or she finds the work boring and wants to change jobs.
questions.explain: 推断题。第五段以西安那位压饼二十六年的女士为例，说明她能凭面团的声音判断是否需要加水，可见长期只做一道菜的人对该食物有极深的理解，故第三项正确。文中未提收入、常换配方或厌倦工作。

questions.q: The phrase 'social glue' in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to _____.
options: a sweet food that children like
a rule that everyone must follow
a problem that spreads quickly in a crowd
questions.explain: 词义题。第六段紧接说陌生人因排队而交谈、摊主记住你的口味、熟客变成朋友，可见 social glue 指'把人联结在一起的东西'，故选第一项。其余选项与上下文不符。
